title: A FATHER'S GIFT, A DAUGHTER'S BOLDNESS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And Caleb said, "I will give my daughter Aksah in marriage to the man who attacks and captures Kiriath Sepher." Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, took it; so Caleb gave his daughter Aksah to him in marriage. One day when she came to Othniel, she urged him to ask her father for a field. When she got off her donkey, Caleb asked her, "What can I do for you?" - Josh 15:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A tender family scene unfolds inside all these borders and battles. Caleb offers his daughter Achsah in marriage to whoever captures Kiriath Sepher, and his own nephew Othniel — who would later become one of Israel's judges — rises to the challenge. Then Achsah herself steps forward with boldness, coming to her father with a request. Caleb, the mighty warrior, turns to his daughter and gently asks, "What can I do for you?"

There is something beautiful in this glimpse of Caleb the father. The same man who faced giants without flinching bends down to hear the desire of his daughter's heart. His strength in battle is matched by tenderness at home. And Achsah is not timid; she knows her father's generous heart and comes to him confidently with what she needs.

This small picture points to something greater. We have a Father in heaven whose strength is beyond measure, yet who bends to ask His children, in effect, "What can I do for you?" Jesus taught us to come boldly, asking, seeking, knocking, because our Father delights to give good gifts to His children (Matt 7:11). Like Achsah, we can approach God not with cringing fear but with confident trust, knowing His heart toward us is kind. The mighty God is also a tender Father.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you approach God with the confidence of a beloved child, or with timid fear?
- What good gift might you be hesitating to ask your heavenly Father for?
- How does knowing God's tender heart change the way you pray?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are both mighty and tender toward Your children. Help me to come to You boldly, like Achsah to Caleb, trusting Your generous and loving heart. Amen.
